thesis: Bill Gurley argues that the traditional IPO process is an archaic system designed forty years ago that has not been updated for modern tools, resulting in massive value transfers to investors at the expense of Silicon Valley founders and employees. He contends that this underpricing is a tautological outcome of a broken process driven by a frequency mismatch where founders do one IPO in a lifetime while investment banks and mutual funds execute dozens annually, causing the less experienced founders to fall back on tradition due to anxiety.
